title: Research Data Series: Index of Common Inflation Expectations

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve Board staff published a methodology note for the Index of Common Inflation Expectations (CIE), a dynamic factor model that summarizes comovement across multiple inflation expectations measures. The CIE is published quarterly as an experimental research data series, with updates scheduled for noon Eastern Time on the third Friday of January, April, July, and October. An updated version of the CIE was introduced in April 2022, incorporating additional survey data and methodological refinements, with the original series being phased out by October 2022.
key_points: The CIE is a dynamic factor model summarizing comovement across a wide variety of inflation expectations measures
Original CIE was updated in April 2022 to add the NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations (1-year and 3-year ahead measures) and Michigan Survey percentiles (25th and 75th)
The updated CIE removed the 5-year TIPS breakeven inflation measure as redundant and redefined the Livingston Survey 1-year measure to use a 12-month growth rate
The CIE produces projections onto SPF 10-year PCE inflation and Michigan next 5-10 years inflation
Quarterly updates are posted at noon ET on the third Friday of January, April, July, and October, or the first Friday following an FOMC meeting if that date conflicts
This is explicitly an experimental research series that may be discontinued and should be used for informational purposes only
why_it_matters: The CIE provides a consolidated signal of inflation expectations across multiple surveys and market measures. Market participants and policymakers monitor inflation expectations as a key input for rate path expectations and inflation risk premium assessment. As a Federal Reserve staff research product, it offers a model-based summary of common trends in expectations data.
macro_context: Inflation expectations are a critical input for monetary policy formulation and market pricing. The CIE synthesizes multiple surveys (SPF, Michigan, NY Fed SCE, Livingston) and market-based measures (TIPS breakeven inflation) into a unified indicator. Changes in the CIE could signal shifts in perceived inflation risk or anchoring of expectations, which directly influences Fed policy calculus and real asset pricing.
notes: Source is a Federal Reserve staff methodology note documenting an experimental data series. While related to macro catalysts (inflation expectations are a key macro indicator), this is primarily archival methodology documentation rather than a direct market catalyst. Published March 5, 2021 (historical record). The April 17, 2026 update timestamp at the bottom indicates the data files were refreshed, but the note content itself is dated. Relevant as background/reference for understanding the CIE indicator used in inflation expectations analysis.
